source_construct: L36: _build_signed_string(..., body_digest: str | None, ...) -> tuple[str, datetime | None]
target_translation: func buildSignedString(signedHeaders, method, path string, header func(name string) (string, bool), bodyDigest string, sigData map[string]string) (string, *time.Time, error). bodyDigest is a plain string with "" for None: the only use is the truthiness test at L56, and no caller passes "". The returned signature date is *time.Time, nil when no "(created)" or "date" header is signed; the caller tests it for nil before the 12-hour check. The error result covers what Python raises: a signed header that is missing (KeyError at L65, also "date" at L52 and "(expires)"/"(created)" in sig_data at L48, L62), a bad "created" integer (L48) and an unparsable Date (L52). The checker does not catch these (L229-236 is outside any try), so the error becomes a 500. The header lookup must include Host, because Go keeps Host out of http.Header (r.Host for an incoming request, req.Host or req.URL.Host for an outgoing one), and both callers sign "host" (L330, L332 and remote signers).
